frames.construction: Onfōn can take an accusative material payment, as the directly attested onféngon hig syndrige penegas (Mt20.10). Teach this bounded frame for pęning and māre; the Unit14 dative-receive frame remains valid.
Dōn takes an accusative object and an agreeing predicate gelīc; the comparison person is dative. Direct source Þū dydest hig gelīce ūs (Mt20.12) supports hīe ūs gelīce.
Wið+dative expresses payment/return: wið his dæges weorce; wið ānum pęninge. This is distinct from the prior hostile combat use.
Forgieldan: recipient dative, paid thing accusative. A passive with retained recipient dative is locally scaffolded in28.1.
Wēnan introduces a ðæt-content clause. In this past report sceolden expresses what the workers expected to receive; it is not automatically an obligation.
Eall can strengthen the equative: eall swā micel swā, just as much as. Micel is substantive neuter; the second recipient remains dative under the understood giving verb.

Two bounded accusative frames: gōd ofer persons, kind toward; nis ofer a teacher, not above in rank. In29.8 bare strong accusative plural ungeðancfulle/yfele denote unthankful/evil people; this exact personal-object use is newly taught here and is not inherited from prior bare genitive plural or article+weak adjective syntax. Neither ofer frame is a spatial crossing.
Swęrian with ðurh+accusative names the oath standard. Repeated ne ðurh phrases share the initial negative command.
For+dative in eye for eye/tooth for tooth expresses equivalent exchange. The first noun is nominative in the quoted formula.
Lǣran takes the taught people or taught matter as accusative object in these clauses. Passive teaching plus controlled infinitive remains supplied31.3.
Ālīes takes an accusative person; fram+dative names what the person is released from. Yfele is abstract substantive neuter dative.
